extracted.intended_audience: Army commanders, public affairs officers (OCPA/OASD (PA)), event sponsors, and installation PA staffs
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for Army public affairs support to civilian and military public events (exhibits, ceremonial units, aerial demonstrations, open houses, donations, liaison, and related approvals). Covers approval authorities, safety, procedural requirements, and program objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCONUS performance approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: United States-based Army musical units may perform OCONUS only with prior approval of the OASD (PA), the appropriate OCONUS commander, and the host nation; all requests for OCONUS musical support are referred to the OCPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for OCONUS musical support may be approved only if: (a) the event sponsor sends the request to the unified combatant commander or the OASD (PA) as appropriate; (b) the unified combatant command determines adequate in-theater assets are not available and the event is sufficiently important to warrant CONUS assets; (c) the OASD (PA) evaluates the request and, if approved, forwards it to the appropriate military Service for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremonial units authorization and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Ceremonial units include special or unit color guards, drill teams, and other specialized units appropriate for military and patriotic ceremonies in the civilian domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These units may be (1) activated according to an approved table of organization and equipment or table of distribution and allowances, or (2) composed of volunteers serving in an official or unofficial capacity as authorized by the local commander.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally authorized volunteer units standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for locally authorized volunteer ceremonial units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volunteer units should be well-trained and have professional bearing, and be operated at no additional cost to the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Armed Forces Color Guard composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of a Joint Armed Forces Color Guard for public programs where display of colors is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When available, employ: (1) Two Army flag bearers with national and Army colors; (2) One each Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, and Coast Guard flag bearer with individual Service colors; (3) One Army and one Marine Corps rifleman as escorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color guard seniority and national colors rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules when a Joint Armed Forces Color Guard cannot be formed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The senior member of the senior military Service in the color guard will carry the national colors. Soldiers, when present, will carry the colors since the Army is the senior Service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carrying foreign or nonmilitary flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy on Army personnel carrying flags of foreign nations, veterans groups, or other nonmilitary organizations in public ceremonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army personnel may carry flags of foreign nations in official civil ceremonies when an official of that nation is present in an official capacity and is one for whom honors normally would be rendered. In all other public programs or ceremonies, Army personnel in uniform and in an official capacity are not authorized to carry flags of foreign nations, veterans groups, or other nonmilitary organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army exhibits primary purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary purposes of Army exhibits used to support public affairs programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While exhibits contribute to PA, their primary purpose is to (a) support recruiting and retention efforts, and/or (b) further Army professional, scientific, and technical interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit approval and submission requirements (national/international)
rubrics_metrics.description: OASD (PA) approval required for PA exhibits at national and international events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be forwarded using DD Form 2536, through channels, to the OCPA at least 45 days prior to the date of the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local commander authority for local exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to approve exhibit participation at local events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local commanders, down to and including installation commanders, may approve exhibit participation at local events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted exhibit locations and advertising restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Army exhibits may be displayed and advertising limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibits may be displayed in any location where the general public gathers including commercially owned spaces (e.g., shopping centers, malls) if the exhibit is not used specifically to draw the public to that location. In conjunction with events at shopping centers or malls, Army participation is allowed if such events are sponsored by a civic group and Army participation is not used in advertising or promotional activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loans of Army art and borrower responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy on loaning Army art and responsibilities of the requesting agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The U.S. Army Center of Military History maintains the inventory of Army art, many paintings are packaged into exhibits and available for loan. The requesting agency is responsible for any required indemnification and shipping charges (see AR 870–5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit display duration and indemnity insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Period authorized for exhibits to remain on display and insurance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period authorized is based on the type of event and proper use of Army personnel/resources. Normally, an Army exhibit may remain for the duration of the event. Indemnity insurance is normally only required for Army exhibits described in paragraph referencing art loans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pentagon exhibits policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy governing Armed Forces exhibits displayed in designated Pentagon exhibit space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibits will conform to the regulation; no classified material may be displayed; maximum permissible weight on the Pentagon Concourse is 150 pounds per square foot; only items currently in military inventory or in a service-testing program may be displayed; reference to a commercial concern limited to a standard nameplate on equipment or a 4-by-6-inch plaque crediting the lender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pentagon exhibit request procedures and required data
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and information required when requesting Pentagon exhibit display space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests are forwarded to the OCPA for OASD (PA) approval at least 40 calendar days before the desired display period. Requests must contain: size of area desired (max available 30 ft by 45 ft), time period desired (normally max 1 week), alternate dates, contact person name/office/telephone, special electrical requirements, title and brief description of the exhibit (sound-producing items allowed if volume kept low), a security review statement per paragraph 5–1 (if not cleared, four copies of text/diagrams/sketches/photos and one copy of films/slides/sound tracks must accompany request), and a statement that the display will contain no reference to a commercial concern other than permitted nameplate/plaque.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lending/leasing materiel and facilities policy references
rubrics_metrics.description: References to Army policies governing lending/leasing materiel and facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General Army policy on lending or leasing materiel and facilities is in AR 700–131. Policy on lending to veterans and scouting organizations is in AR 725–1. Policy on lending/selling/donating flags is in AR 840–10. Policy on DA Seal and DA Plaque is in AR 840–1. Policy on private persons/organizations using Army real estate is in AR 405–80. Policy on lending Army property to other USG agencies is in AR 700–131 and AR 735–5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explosives and pyrotechnics participation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy on Army participation in public events involving explosives or pyrotechnics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except in rare cases, participation of Army personnel in public events involving explosives is not advisable because of injury and legal liability. ACOMs may approve such participation when it meets established safety criteria and is clearly in the interest of the Army. Using explosives on military installations is at the discretion of ACOMs; using antique weapons not routinely fired is prohibited (including for national salutes). Restrictions do not apply to routine salutes authorized in AR 600–25. Local commanders may approve rifle and cannon salutes conducted off post as part of an approved PA program if a safety assessment has been done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donation eligibility for obsolete/condemned combat equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations authorized under 10 USC 2572 to acquire obsolete or condemned combat equipment for public display or ceremonial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized recipients include municipal corporations; Soldiers’ Monument associations; state museums; incorporated museums operated for educational purposes only (no profit); local posts of VFW, American Legion, or recognized war veterans associations; recognized foreign war veterans association units; and posts of the Sons of Veterans Reserve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veterans organization recognition criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria used to recognize veterans associations for purposes of acquiring property by donation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition is based on size and purpose of the organization and services rendered to veterans (if composed of honorably discharged members). Services rendered include informing veterans and family members of employment rights and benefits, and actions on behalf of disabled veterans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donation application requirements for local veterans posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Information local posts/chapters/units must submit to obtain eligibility and request donations of obsolete/condemned property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Their national headquarters must submit eligibility requests to OASD (PA) containing: citation/copy of act granting charter or recognition, statement outlining association’s purpose and intended use of property, names/titles/addresses of all officers, copy of last financial statement, copy of constitution/charter/bylaws, and total membership. Once eligibility determined, requests for donations are submitted to Commander AMSTA–IM–OER and local requests should include written approval from national headquarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aerial activities definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of aerial demonstrations and aerial activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes performances by DOD demonstration team (Golden Knights), flyovers, command parachute demonstration teams, tactical demonstrations, aerial reviews, static displays, and other aerial activities as defined in DODD 5410.18 and DODI 5410.19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for Army aerial demonstrations — safety and altitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety is the primary consideration for Army aerial demonstrations and specific altitude and regulatory compliance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All pertinent safety regulations of FAA, USPA, DOD, and DA will be rigidly observed and take precedence over other conditions. Flyovers performed under this regulation will not be flown lower than FAA-regulated altitudes and in no case flown less than 500 feet above ground level. Flyovers must comply with all applicable FAA regulations unless a waiver is obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: No additional cost to the U.S. Government for aerial demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost policy for aerial demonstrations at public events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aerial demonstrations (excluding those by the DOD demonstration teams) at public events, including OCONUS, will be provided at no additional cost to the U.S. Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying air shows criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria an air show must meet for Army participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Air shows must: (a) ensure logistical support does not interfere with official duties or readiness; (b) serve Army community relations and legitimate Army PA/training interests; (c) involve the Army in the best interest of DOD; (d) be of interest/benefit to the local civilian community, the providing Army command, or DOD; (e) the ACOM/organization must be able/willing to provide similar support to comparable events by similar non-Federal entities; (f) participation must not be restricted by statute or regulation; (g) no admission fee (beyond reasonable sponsoring costs) charged for the event or the portion supported by DOD/Army, or Army support must be incidental to the entire event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in fund-raising or charity air shows
rubrics_metrics.description: When aerial demonstrations may be performed at fund-raising or charity air shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aerial demonstrations may be performed at broadly based fund-raising air shows or those sponsored by broadly based charities/nonprofits focusing on the community as a whole when Army/DOD support is incidental; for-profit organizations may be eligible if they donate at least half of any excess event revenues to local broadly based community organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD demonstration team (Golden Knights) performance policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Special policies pertaining to aerial performances by the Golden Knights demonstration team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appearances on a military installation, including joint-use airfields, will be approved only in support of an official open house or similar public event; all activities likely to result in national media exposure (videos, orientation flights, TV appearances) will be reported to OCPA; cost analyses will be conducted at the conclusion of the demonstration season and forwarded to the Secretary of the Army through OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army demonstration teams (non-Golden Knights) performance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for aerial demonstrations by Army demonstration teams and aircraft other than the Golden Knights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrations depend on Army's ability to provide resources at event time. Activities such as mass parachute jumps, aerial delivery of equipment, aircraft assault demonstrations, and tactical helicopter troop landings under simulated tactical conditions will not be performed at CONUS public events without prior approval by OCPA, DCS, G–3/5/7 Aviation, and Vice Chief of Staff. When aircraft are on static display, qualified military personnel must be available to answer questions; placards describing basic specifications/missions encouraged. Flight demonstrations involving several maneuvers should include a narrator provided by the appropriate unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gubernatorial inauguration flyover conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which State ARNG aircraft may perform flyovers of gubernatorial inaugurations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flyovers are authorized only when flown in conjunction with a previously scheduled training mission and at no additional Federal expense; the governor's office must request the flyover in writing; participating aircraft limited to ARNG resources assigned to that State/Territory (States may not request ARNG aircraft from another State); the flyover must be a single type of aircraft in a single, straight and level flight over a fixed point without aerobatics; limited to up to four aircraft and one Service component; multiple flyovers or aerial reviews are prohibited; flyover must occur during the actual inauguration ceremony at a patriotic juncture; States must coordinate with appropriate Federal and State aviation agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flyovers suspension and exceptions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy suspending flyover support in the civilian domain and criteria for exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To conserve personnel, aircraft, and flying hours, the Army has suspended flyover support in the civilian domain. Exceptions will be granted only in rare circumstances for exceptional high impact events that meet specific strategic communication requirements. Exceptions are considered by OCPA and, when appropriate, OASD (PA) on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions request content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Information required when requesting exceptions to aerial policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests forwarded through command channels must include: character and significance of the event; recruiting benefits and involvement; expected media attendance and coverage; other military participation planned (e.g., bands or color guards); unit to conduct flyover if approved; impact if flyover not approved; specific benefits that cannot be achieved by any other form of military participation; in the interest of safety, risk assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition and admission charge prohibitions for aerial assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibitions on competing for prize money and charging admission related to Army aerial assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army aerial assets (including parachute demonstration teams) may not compete for prize money. Charges for admission to Army aircraft or other equipment are specifically prohibited. The sale of photos of attendees seated in Army aircraft or equipment is also prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aerial demonstration duration and type restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on duration and number/type scheduling of aerial demonstrations at events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army aerial demonstrations normally limited to 2 days at any one aerial event; parachute demonstrations may extend to a 3-day period. Waivers may be granted when extended participation does not compromise another event due to travel time, the audience will change each day, or the event is national/international and in the Army's best interest. Normally, no two aerial demonstrations of the same type will be approved for a single public event; exceptions when DOD teams perform and other demos are on different days. Aircraft performance record demonstrations restricted to aircraft assigned to an operational unit for at least 6 months; demonstrations implying competition among Services are not authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and responsibilities of controllers for demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to designate an Army controller and the controller's responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a flyover or demonstration involves only Army aircraft, a nonparticipating Army aviator will be designated to act as an Army controller. When two or more Services participate, the military coordinating commander will designate a senior military controller. The controller is responsible for coordinating between event sponsor and Armed Forces participants and ensuring flight and safety regulations of the military departments and the FAA are observed. Safety and operational procedures are in AR 95–1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flying time and readiness use guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle that flying time devoted to aircraft participation must be useful to readiness/training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flying time devoted to aircraft participation will be used to the fullest extent for combat readiness or training purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assault aircraft and helicopter troop landing restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on assault aircraft demonstrations and helicopter troop landings under simulated tactical conditions when conducted for public viewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such demonstrations are restricted to military installations capable of supporting those activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAA waiver requirement for public demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement for event sponsors to obtain FAA waivers for public demonstrations by military aircraft or parachutists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The event sponsor is required to obtain an FAA waiver. Final authorization depends on the sponsor securing a waiver far enough in advance to permit planning. An FAA waiver is normally required at least 60 days prior to the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of resources and recruiting coordination for aerial demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Support depends on resources and coordination to maximize recruiting benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support to aerial demonstrations depends on availability of resources. Maximum advantage for Army recruiting will be taken at public events where aerial demonstrations are authorized; coordination should be made with the appropriate Army recruiting battalion advertising and PA office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for approval of aerial activities and required forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Who must approve aerial support and required submission forms/systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for aerial support must be submitted on DD Form 2535 and/or electronically through the Defense Outplacement Referral System (DORS). Requesters must obtain OCPA approval for all aerial support for events in the civilian domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for submission of aerial support requests
rubrics_metrics.description: How to submit requests for various types of aerial activities and required content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All requests from event sponsors for Army aerial support in the civilian domain will be submitted for processing and approval to OCPA on DD Form 2535 and/or electronically through DORS. Aircraft performance record demonstrations require submissions including (1) description of the aircraft, (2) justification for the proposed record attempt, and (3) supporting flight and PA plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Golden Knights scheduling and submission timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule and deadline for requests for demonstrations by the Golden Knights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All requests for Golden Knights demonstrations will be submitted electronically through DORS to OCPA prior to 30 September of the year prior to the event. An Army scheduling conference is conducted each October for the following year; requests must be submitted by 30 September to be evaluated at the conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and procedures for flyover exceptions and infiltration/exfiltration demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Special approval routes and required concurrence for flyovers and aerial infiltration/exfiltration demonstrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for flyover exceptions must be approved by the Vice Chief of Staff of the Army through OCPA and submitted via DORS and/or DD Form 2535. Aerial infiltration and exfiltration demonstrations must be approved by the Vice Chief of Staff of the Army through OCPA and submitted by DORS/DD Form 2535. These demonstrations may be considered if Army participants are properly qualified and, for aerial rappelling demonstrations, commanders ensure compliance with safety and operational requirements of AR 95–1, FM 3–21.38, and other pertinent regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement official programs (list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of command-initiated official programs effective in informing the public about the Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official programs include: an active speakers bureau program; ongoing liaison with organizations at local/state/regional events; participatory membership in civic, business, and professional organizations; using exhibits, bands, color guards, and other ceremonial units in the public domain; periodic open houses and installation tour programs; participating in national holiday observances; supporting overseas host-nation activities (American youth, holiday, and traditional programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial programs guidance for personnel participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance encouraging unofficial community participation by military personnel and family members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs involving direct contact with the civilian community are effective for improving community relations. Commanders should encourage military and civilian personnel and family members to participate as private persons in local community activities. Military personnel lending voluntary support during off-duty time to community activities may be authorized to participate in uniform if consistent with DOD 5500.7–R (see AR 670–1 for appropriate off-duty uniform wear).

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison responsibilities with civilian persons and organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commander duties to maintain continual liaison with local community persons and organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders must: develop effective two-way communication channels between Army and community; foster cooperation among civilian and military agencies; sponsor joint social activities; provide adequate off-post housing, public facilities, entertainment, and services to military personnel and Family without regard to protected characteristics; provide maximum support of Army activities (e.g., AFD/AFW); exchange clergy and chaplains; provide recreational facilities for Service personnel within community; support Army recruiting mission and community understanding of enlistment benefits; participate in/host civic, professional, and business clubs; promote USMA and ROTC scholarship opportunities through educators/counselors; promote use of ARNG armories or USAR centers by civic organizations. Official civilian advisory committees/councils must comply with AR 15–1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal community relations working groups minimum functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for formation and minimum functions of informal community relations working groups managed by the PAO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forums should be composed of installation personnel and their civilian counterparts. Minimum functions: plan a continuous community relations program; establish and maintain contact with civilian service, business, economic, professional, minority, and veterans organizations; establish and maintain contact with key civilian community officials; evaluate possible effects of command operations and policies on community relations and advise the commander of actions to reduce/prevent adverse reaction; maintain a consistent orientation program on community relations for all members of the command; promote new ways for members to participate in local community activities; conduct a periodic appraisal of public attitudes toward the command to determine need for modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community survey and analysis guidance and legal cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of community surveys and analyses in developing public engagement programs with caution on legal constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community surveys and analyses are helpful; FM 3–61.1 provides guidance. Caution must be taken to ensure surveys do not violate FOIA, the Privacy Act, or AR 380–13 concerning acquisition and storage of information on nonaffiliated persons/organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund-raising support policy and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: When Army support may be provided for fund-raising and related limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army support may be provided to United, federated, or Joint fund-raising campaigns authorized by AR 600–29; other appeals authorized by the President or Director, OPM; efforts sponsored by military Service aid societies. Army support for local fund-raising governed by DOD 5500.7–R and Joint Ethics Regulation. Volunteer efforts by Army personnel as private individuals are encouraged. Fund-raising concerts by military bands will be limited to those sponsored by or held to benefit authorized campaigns; exceptions may be made if Department of the Army determines benefits are sufficiently widespread. Commanders of combatant commands may authorize exceptions in overseas areas (except Hawaii and Alaska) to permit participation in athletic/sports competition within their commands to support local fundraising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observance of the Army Birthday guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance regarding observance of the Army Birthday (June 14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: June 14 is observed as the anniversary of the founding of the U.S. Army. Guidance on public events in the regulation applies to Army Birthday observances. Commanders are encouraged to remind personnel of traditions by reading the Resolution of the Continental Congress at troop formations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Armed Forces Day and Veterans Day support policy
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD/Army policy for supporting Armed Forces Day (AFD) and Veterans Day observances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD policy is to provide military support for AFD and Veterans Day observances at communities designated as official DOD regional sites and for smaller local observances as resources permit. Major ACOMs have authority to approve military flyovers for AFD and Veterans Day when the event occurs within 7 calendar days of the official holiday date. Special AFD commemorative editions of unit/installation newspapers may be published to stress Army contributions; editions may include messages from commanders and special features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential wreath-laying ceremony policy and representative reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: OASD (PA) policy on placing presidential wreaths and responsibilities for Presidential representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OASD (PA) governs placing presidential wreaths. Army elements at appendix H are responsible for developing an appropriate ceremony and providing a Presidential representative to place a wreath. General officer is the minimum rank of a designated Presidential representative except when practical considerations preclude availability. Army elements must provide OCPA with name, rank, title, address, and telephone number of the designated representative on a continuing basis as shown in the quarterly report schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open house definition and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and purpose of an open house as a military program inviting the general public onto an installation or facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An open house is designed to present military missions, equipment, facilities, and personnel to a local or regional civilian community to satisfy public interest and establish cordial relationships. It may coincide with AFD, Army Birthday, branch birthdays, anniversaries, community events, or media day. Installation commanders are encouraged to hold at least one open house annually within available resources and operational limits. Displays/events should come from the host installation or local community except that equipment/personnel may be invited from other installations to demonstrate capabilities not found locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open house participation and spectator activity guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on target audiences and suitable spectator participation activities for open houses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open houses should encourage attendance and participation by family groups. Spectator participation events such as vehicle rides, junior jump towers, vision devices, communications equipment, physical fitness skills, and first aid techniques that appeal to children are considered proper. Discretion should be used regarding spectator participation events related to violent aspects of combat training; improper events are listed (text continues in next paragraphs).
